messages.author: 04b15f8a5125f402
messages.subject: Barrier Model ignoring range?
parts:
I've been working on a model of a river. The specification for the model is nearly identical to the barrier model in Krainski et al 2020 (ch 5), but using non-separable time as a grouping effect (like ch 7). 

The barrier is defined as:
MatRange depends upon the exact run, but varies between 100 and 1000 m, all of which  result in identical looking output figures. At present, MatSig is set at 1/2 MatRange. The attached figure happens to have been generated with a range of 500 m.

barrier.model=inla.barrier.pcmatern(mesh,barrier.triangles=barrier.tri,
    prior.range=c(MatRange,0.5),
    prior.sigma=c(MatSig,0.05) )
inlamode="experimental"
inla.setOption(num.threads=NCore, inla.mode=inlamode, mkl=TRUE)

spde=barrier.model
iset=inla.spde.make.index('i',n.spde=spde$f$n,n.group=k)
A=inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh,loc=coordinates(sensorData.sp),group=sensorData.sp$nt2hour)

formula=y~0+Intercept+f(i,model=spde,group=i.group,control.group=list(model='rw2',cyclic=TRUE, hyper=hyperprec, scale.model=FALSE, adjust.for.con.comp=TRUE))


computelist=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, q=FALSE, waic=TRUE, smtp="pardiso", graph=FALSE, config=FALSE, mlik=FALSE, return.marginals=FALSE, return.marginals.predictor=FALSE, po=FALSE, hyperpar=FALSE, openmp.strategy="huge")
controlinla=list(int.strategy="eb") #,strategy="gaussian")

res.hrBarrier=inla(formula,
    data=inla.stack.data(sdat),
    control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, A=inla.stack.A(sdat)),
    inla.mode=inlamode,
    family="gaussian",
    control.inla=controlinla,
    control.family=list(hyper=list(theta=prec.prior)),
    control.compute=computelist,
    num.threads=NCore
    )

For some reason, all outcomes look very similar, with a homogeneous field of 0s at all mesh points except those directly adjacent to my sensor locations (this may be difficult to see in the low-res jpg -- I can attache an SVG if needed, it's just large). This pattern does not change, regardless of what I do with my range in barrier.model. 

 My gut is telling me it's because of how long/skinny the sample region is, or am I missing something?



I plot the result exactly as done in ch7 of Karinski et al.

Any recommendations?

Thanks!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Barrier Model ignoring range?
parts:
Hi,

That’s a really difficult domain to work with.
For the barrier model to work as intended there, you will need to have enough triangles to get multiple triangles across the narrow width, I.e. the inner max.edge for the mesh needs to be clearly smaller than the width.

I’m not sure what you mean by MatSig being half MatRange; they control completely different aspects of the covariate (std.dev. and spatial range) and you also use different probabilities in the specification.

Getting the same results for different MatRange could mean simply that the data is informative enough to overrule the prior. But I would start by looking at the mesh, to ensure that it’s sufficient to represent the model properly.
I assume you use inla.nonconvex.hull() to construct the outer mesh boundary?


Finn

messages.author: 04b15f8a5125f402
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Barrier Model ignoring range?
parts:
I appreciate the help.

I've tried a ton of values for the standard deviation, ranging from very small, to my latest attempt  -- 1/2 the range.
I think at some point, I mistakenly interpreted it to be the standard deviation of the range, which doesn't make sense since the probability is specified. 
Now that I've actually thought about it, I will use a more sensible value.

The mesh was generated using inla.mesh.2d:

boundary <- list(
as.inla.mesh.segment(land.sp),
    NULL)

mesh.loc <- sensors.sp
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc=mesh.loc,
                     boundary=boundary,
                     max.edge=c(10, 100),
                     min.angle=c(30, 21),
                     max.n=c(48000, 16000), ## Safeguard against large meshes.
                     max.n.strict=c(128000, 128000), ## Don't build a huge mesh!
                     cutoff=2, ## Filter away adjacent points.
                     offset=c(12, 60),
                     crs='EPSG:6417'
)

sensor.sp is the sensor locations, the boundary using a land shape that is larger than the study reach.

I basically create barrier by removing the water area from the land:
land.water.sp=gDifference(land.sp, water.sp)

water.tri=inla.over_sp_mesh(x=land.water.sp, y=mesh, type="centroid", ignore.CRS=TRUE)
water.tri.num=length(mesh$graph$tv[,1])
barrier.tri=setdiff(1:water.tri.num, water.tri)
poly.barrier=inla.barrier.polygon(mesh, barrier.triangles=barrier.tri)

barrier.model=inla.barrier.pcmatern(mesh,barrier.triangles=barrier.tri,
prior.range=c(MatRange,0.5),
prior.sigma=c(MatSig,0.05) )

I believe this followed the example in Krainski ch 5. Should I be using the nonconvex hull instead?


That's good to know, thank you. I may need to revisit the covariance.

Thanks for the prompt reply.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Barrier Model ignoring range?
parts:
I would use inla.nonconvex.hull to construct the outer mesh boundary instead of using the default convex hull extension. The convex hull extension has a shape that doesn’t really match the domain of interest. The inner boundary could also likely be made more similar to the actual domain shape.
But the resolution of the inner part looks like it may be sufficient.
However, I’m not sure having the sensor locations as mesh nodes helps or hinders.
Try making the mesh without giving it the sensor locations, so that it only uses the specified boundary/boundaries.
Also, run the model with a regular pcmatern model to see what happens. (Just make sure the outer boundary isn’t too close to the domain of interest.)

Finn

﻿Hi,

That’s a really difficult domain to work with.

I would use inla.nonconvex.hull to construct the outer mesh boundary instead of using the default convex hull extension. The convex hull extension has a shape that doesn’t really match the domain of interest. The inner boundary could also likely be made more similar to the actual domain shape.
But the resolution of the inner part looks like it may be sufficient.
However, I’m not sure having the sensor locations as mesh nodes helps or hinders.
Try making the mesh without giving it the sensor locations, so that it only uses the specified boundary/boundaries.
Also, run the model with a regular pcmatern model to see what happens. (Just make sure the outer boundary isn’t too close to the domain of interest.)

Finn

On 5 Oct 2022, at 23:07, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hi,

That’s a really difficult domain to work with.
For the barrier model to work as intended there, you will need to have enough triangles to get multiple triangles across the narrow width, I.e. the inner max.edge for the mesh needs to be clearly smaller than the width.

I’m not sure what you mean by MatSig being half MatRange; they control completely different aspects of the covariate (std.dev. and spatial range) and you also use different probabilities in the specification.

Getting the same results for different MatRange could mean simply that the data is informative enough to overrule the prior. But I would start by looking at the mesh, to ensure that it’s sufficient to represent the model properly.
I assume you use inla.nonconvex.hull() to construct the outer mesh boundary?


Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Barrier Model ignoring range?
parts:
We have not considered any non-separable covariance/precision model in the SPDE book. What we have there are spatio-temporal (some use to say interaction) models based on the Kronecker product of the precision/covariance between temporal and spatial ones that gives separable precision/covariance.

The terminology problem starts when one uses the inseparability at the mean level (u_{st} cannot splits into u_s + u_t) of the spatio-temporal (interaction: u_{st}) models and gets confused with non-separable precision/covariance (non-separability at a second order property of the model). Thus what we have in the book are spatio-temporal interaction (inseparability at the mean level) but separable precision/covariance models.

The good news is that we are close to having a class of non-stationary and non-separable models implemented and available for the users.

best regards,
Elias
